utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please wait for the entire question. In Sarajevo, in one of the ten Sarajevo municipalities?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You completed elementary school in Trnovo and secondary and teachers high school in the academy of pedagogy in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you performed your civic duty in terms of serving in the Yugoslav Peoples Army in 1970. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Until 1982 you worked as a teacher in the Trnovo school?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: From 1982 until 1990, you worked in Trnovo as the chief of the police station.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: From 1990 until the 21st of April, 1992 you were an inspector for general crime in the public security station of the Trnovo municipality.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Judges what happened on the 21st of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Until April -- 21st of April, 1992, the police in Trnovo worked together, it was a multi-ethnic police force, Serb and Muslim. On the 21st of April, a police patrol out on traffic duties was attacked by the Green Berets when three policemen were killed. Among them was one Serb and two Muslims. That's when the police split into a Serb and Muslim part, because the police officers who were at the police station, Serbs, did not feel safe any longer, and they split off from the station. They left the station. And that was when a separate Serb police station was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So what did you become after that?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: As I already said in response to your question, as I was the chief of the Trnovo municipality police station until the 21st of April, the other officers asked me to be their chief in view of my experience so that they could self-organise and protect their families and households in the eventuality of any disagreements with the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how long were you the Trnovo police station chief?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was the Trnovo police station chief until the 31st of July, 1992. In the meantime, in the villages, outlying villages, in the Trnovo municipality, which were mostly under the control of the Muslim forces, a vast number of crimes occurred. From the 3rd of June until the 7th of July, 1992, more than 100 civilians were killed, mostly the elderly and the infirm and then a few children as well. In the village of Ledici there was an attack carried out on the 3rd of June. It was an ethnically pure Serb village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton is on her feet. Please stop. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would submit that is not only irrelevant, but the question that was asked was actually effectively answered by the witness when he said he was Trnovo police station chief until the 31st of July, 1992. So it has been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us deal with the relevance aspect. What do you say to that, Mr. Tapuskovic? The evidence about the number of civilians being killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can repeat what I have already said many times before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us hear it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I talked about it many times before, throughout this period and particularly during the mandate of Mr. Dragomir Milosevic, during the time that he was on duty, I insisted on a question or a topic or a problem that the intensity of combat of both sides, particularly the combat of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, during the subject period relating to Dragomir Milosevic, asserting that, if I can put it that way, the activities of the SRK - and this is what was the subject of my discussion, and we were supposed to speak about the activities of the SRK - was a response to the activities of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this was not a question of attacks on civilians. And that victims in the territory under the control of the SRK are indicative of the intensity of the combat operations or actions undertaken by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This refers to the entire period from 1992 until 1995, and in particular, to the period pertaining to the duties of Mr. Dragomir Milosevic, when he was performing that duty. I wanted to show a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I believe you would also go on to say that your case is that the intensity of the fighting precludes the existence of a campaign of shelling and sniping, as you have said before, and you also argue that the number of victims is indicative of this intensity and that the SRK was responding to attacks by the ABiH. So there you have it, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, with respect, Your Honour, my submission would be that that argument may be valid if the evidence at issue is reasonably proximate in time to the period of the indictment and this isn't the case at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But 1992 is also pleaded in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have the adjudicated facts from the Galic case. And at this stage, we are not determining the weight that the Chamber will attach to the evidence. We're determining its admissibility on the basis of its relevance, and I would rule that it is relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But I should say at the same time, Mr. Tapuskovic, that the sooner you move to 1994/1995, which are the critical years, then the Chamber would be the better for that. We would profit more from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do want to do that, but I received a number of documents from the Prosecution and that is why I have to dwell on this, on the documents, the Prosecution will probably insist on the documents or rely on the documents in their cross-examination, so I have to cover that for several reasons, but I'm not obliged to explain. One of the documents that I received from the Prosecution yesterday, in view of what the witness has just said about the civilians who were killed at that time, I would like to show that to the witness. And the witness hasn't even seen the documents because I received it late. Perhaps he wouldn't have even mentioned it, but it's a document that I placed on the list a little bit earlier, because I just received it a little bit earlier, and that is document-- I have the Prosecution number, 00731702. And I would happen kindly ask to have the document placed on the ELMO. The first paragraph mentions something that this witness has also experienced. All of these are things that can be of importance in order to evaluate certain topics that are relevant for that entire period from 1992 until 1995. Perhaps the witness can read the first paragraph. If you permit that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at the document, and what does it say in this first paragraph. Can you please read that to the Judges and can you please tell us if you lived through that report on a carried-out investigation. Slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: "Drafted on the 28th of July, 1993 at 1130 hours, at the village cemetery in the village of Milje municipality of Trnovo, at the location where the grave of Borise Ivanovic, son of Alekse and mother Janje nee Bozovic was found, who was born on the 12th of February, 1912 in the village of Milje, municipality of Trnovo and killed on the 15th of June, 1992 by members of the Muslim Ustasha formations by his house in the said village and a certain time after the killing was buried by the so-called Muslim commission for clearing the terrain at the village cemetery in the village of Milje."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who this is?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is my father, who was killed on the 15th of June, 1992 in the yard of his family house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now can you please tell us where you were for a certain amount of time after you stopped being the chief of police in July 1992, as you've said?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 31st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you for a short period of time?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: For a short period of time I was in Kalinovik because the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina had captured the entire area of the Trnovo municipality on the 30th and the 31st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know anything about the Lukavac 93 action and can you please briefly describe it and tell us when it took place?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Lukavac 93 action, I know about. It was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, I'm sorry. Your Honour, with respect to the Lukavac -- is mention of the Lukavac 1993 action, I'm actually guided by Your Honour's ruling last month with respect to the 65 ter summaries in which you said that where applicable the -- you said: "Considering that this further information should include at least information on the occupation of the witness during the relevant period, the rank of the witness, his unit, where applicable, locations the witness will discuss and the specific events the witness will discuss." I'm guided by this in rising and saying Lukavac 1993 was never disclosed as any part of the information that this witness would testify about. So I would object to this evidence. I have had no notice in that record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, the Chamber does not agree that the purpose of asking for a summary is to exclude evidence that is not in it. That's not the purpose of it. Secondly, it's only a summary, and where, as in this case, the Chamber concludes that the evidence is relevant, the Chamber will allow it, and it will allow this evidence. If you find that you are embarrassed, you may exceptionally seek some redress from the Chamber, but I stress "exceptionally." That redress may take the form of the Chamber allowing you a little more time to do some further research. I'm not encouraging it. I myself don't think it is warranted in this case, and I would not allow it. Proceed, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will take into account my learned friend's objection and move on to the issue at hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- well, you said you were a policeman. In the following months until the war was over, did you at any point stop being a policeman?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I remained a policeman until the end of the war. I worked in the Kula police station. I was transferred there on the 2nd of November, 1992. It was the centre of public security station in Lukavica. I was a crime inspector there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: With which department?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The public security department within the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since you worked with the matters of public security, were there any other types of policemen there in the station?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the public security station at Kula, there was a detention unit or a detention facility there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just a second. We'll get there, but let us not hurry. In the police, you worked on crime within the domain of public security. Were there any other police forces?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the crime squad, we had uniformed police also from the public security sector. I think there were some 60 to 70 of them in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In order for us to understand the whole situation and in order for you to be able to explain better, I have to show you a map, which is document 2872.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the southern part, the area of Lukavica, as the witness said. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you indicate where the police station was, the one you mentioned? And put a circle there.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I need to get my bearings first. I think it is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Where was Kula?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the same place, in the vicinity there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the separation lines approximately at the time you arrived there, the separation lines between the VRS and the 1st corps of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do I need to draw lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is very difficult for me to navigate here, but it was something like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That suffices. If we considered this regarding the elevations there, what was your position like there?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Kula and Lukavica were below the Mojmilo elevation, which dominates the area. I don't know what the exact altitude is. It is a ridge. There is also Mount Igman, where the ABiH forces were. It had a commanding view over the entire area of Kula, Lukavica and Bijelo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the ridge, as you called it, at Mojmilo, as best you can?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Mojmilo ridge, I know very well is above the settlement of Alipasino and onwards to Vraca, more or less like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a good look at the map. You see some things there?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is very difficult for me to navigate this map, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Then mark it as you think it is.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think this is so. This is the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But the ridge of the hill, the ridge of the Mojmilo elevation.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't get my bearings here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic, the witness obviously has a difficulty finding his bearings on this map, but this red circle, he was talking about Lukavica, but he forgot to write Kula. I would like to see Kula on the map. Could you please also note some letters on all this for the confrontation line, maybe put an L or something, and for the ridge also, so we can find our way later on, because right now I'm also losing my bearings. Starting with Kula, please, Witness, can you tell us where Kula is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the encircled part. Close to where our police station was place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Mindua, perhaps I can ask the witness to mark the circle with a K.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Maybe place a K, like Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As for the blue line, please put an L there.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I won't press any further, but please have a good look at the line at the top. There is some inscription here. This is the part that you referred to as Mojmilo. I don't want to force you to mark anything you are unable to, but have another look, please.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mojmilo dominates over the settlement of Nedzarici, which is at the foot of Mojmilo hill and its elevation. That's where Nedzarici is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the elevations. Maybe you can find it somewhere on the map, where the name is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The lettering is very small. I cannot read.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the central part of the map. Please zoom in.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we zoom in, we'll lose the current markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You still cannot see anything?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us save this map first as such. I wish to tender it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D283, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us zoom in now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see now? Can you read the things on the map, an elevation perhaps?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can I encircle the elevation?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is this Mojmilo and the ridge that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the ridge. The elevation is 680 metres above sea level. I saw it finally. It overlooks the settlement of Lukavica, Kula, parts of Dobrinja IV and Dobrinja I, in the hands of Serbian forces, and in particular, overlooks the settlement of Nedzarici, which was an encirclement. It was in the Serbian hands. I can tell that you in the settlement of Nedzarici, many members of my family resided. Nedzarici saw daily, fierce attacks, and many of my family and relatives were killed in Nedzarici. Since many of my relatives on my wife's side lived in Nedzarici. Her brother was killed there, her mother was wounded, my aunt was killed by a sniper in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, is it necessary for me to tender this, since many witnesses have already explained to us and marked Mojmilo on other occasions? Therefore, I do not believe it is necessary to tender this document as such. Rather, I will continue with my questions to Mr. Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said you worked in the general crime section but that there were also some 80 other policemen, more or less, who worked in the public security sector. Can you tell the Judges whether on occasion those policemen and you as a civilian working for the police participated in the combat activities of the SRK?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: There were situations when the front line was under threat, the front line of the army of Republika Srpska, and that's when orders would arrive that both us and the uniformed police would be engaged at certain lines in order to help members of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The police forces in that form with that number and you who were members of the public security service, what sort of weapons did you have at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The police station where I was deployed just had infantry weapons. It didn't use any other type of weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And since you were there since 1992, at the time when you got to Kula, were there any other kinds of weapons that were used by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, other than the weapons that you had at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that the army of Republika Srpska in that area had heavy weapons as well, artillery weapons. Cannon, mortars. I know they had them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly so then we can deal with the time relevant to the indictment, but since you were there in 1992 and 1993 can you tell us if you recall in 1993 what the combat was like in the area where you were at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In late 1992 and 1993, there were frequent battles along the line of separation. There was shelling by the B and H army. I recall a date, I think it was either the 14th or the 15th of March, 1993, and this was in the vicinity of the public security station. That was where the Kula prison was, the KP Kula prison, where there were detainees of the army of Republika Srpska too who had been sent there on orders of the army command because they had committed various misdemeanours or violations. I don't know what kind of violations they were. I'm not sure whether on the 14th or the 15th of March, the area where we were was shelled, where our public security station was, and the prison also, I think it was a mortar shell, and it killed nine detainees of the army of Republika Srpska and wounded two guards because they happened to be in the compound when the detainees were taking their daily walk. Besides the prisoners who were killed, I think another 13 were wounded, and these were detainees of the army of Republika Srpska, which, as I said, were detained because they had committed certain army -- violations of certain army regulations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton. Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my submission with respect to this evidence at this point would be that in order for it to be considered relevant, my friend would have to point to actually which of the adjudicated facts it might go to. My quick review of the adjudicated facts doesn't reveal anything that this evidence relates to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: To what does this evidence relate?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, today when I was explaining upon your instructions what it was important about what I was asking the witness here, I didn't mention any adjudicated facts. I mentioned them yesterday and one more time. Here, I was just speaking in general in relation to the entire period and it had nothing to do with the adjudicated facts. As Defence attorney, I intend to expand certain things contained in the adjudicated facts and I tend to -- intend to dispute some and expand others with new evidence. I did not mention adjudicated facts today. I mentioned one of them yesterday about which I believe there should be no dispute, so I just intend to expand on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just tell us what it relates to, how it is relevant. Never mind adjudicated facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, precisely what the witness was talking about, what was happening in Nedzarici, and I even stopped him from mentioning all of them, but he mentioned as series of his relatives who fell victim in Nedzarici and again he spoke about detainees who were in the prison and who were killed. These were nine people and many were wounded as well. What I'm trying to do now is present the idea that the victims in the territory controlled by the SRK an indicator of the combat actions undertaken by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and all of that in the context that the objective of the army of Republika Srpska was not to cause terror in that part of Sarajevo which was under the control of the Bosnia and Herzegovina army but that it was a response to activities of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and not a campaign of attack on civilians. What you heard from the witness indicates what the situation was like in terms of victims at positions held by the SRK and in Nedzarici, which constitutes the heart of the town as well as Lukavica, which is also a part of the town. This is what we're saying, that the events, the victims, on the side and territory that was under the command of the SRK is evidence of the intensity of combat actions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, this is nothing -- so the intensity argument relates back to 1992/1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the indictment against Dragomir Milosevic was amended a month before the trial began. It was expanded to a time-period during which he was not a commander and that he inherited the campaign from his predecessor, the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, thus I'm forced to deal with that time-period as well, and to indicate that in that time-period as well some things did not proceed in the way reported in the adjudicated facts, especially not during the time when he was commander and particularly in the time-period from August to May, the period from August 1994 to May 1995, and then the fighting intensified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm not following you now, because you said previously that you were not relying on the adjudicated facts to establish the relevance of this evidence, so I presume you're establishing it on some other means. Because, Ms. Edgerton, is it your submission that evidence of the 1992/1993 period is only relevant if it is founded on an adjudicated fact?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I would certainly concede that a certain amount of this evidence is relevant by way of context. Your Honours will recall that we produced the report and -- of Dr. Donia, who testified here with a contextual paper on the evidence. However, most of the 1992/1993 evidence, Your Honours, is linked with the adjudicated facts, we'd submit. So there is -- there's a certain amount that goes to context, Your Honours, the broader context. And that, I think, has to be judged on a case-by-case basis since we're rising only on a case-by-case basis, but generally the relevance of the pre-indictment period is directly linked to the adjudicated facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You don't found the relevance of this particular evidence, Mr. Tapuskovic, on adjudicated facts. I understand you to be establishing it on another basis, and this seems to have something to do with the -- the general state of terror. Explain that to me now. How -- how is what happened in 1992/1993 relevant to this question of terror in the indictment which relates to 1994/1995? Having explained that, we'll take the break. No. I said having, after he has explained that. It's probably a wrong use of the past participle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as the Defence counsel for Dragomir Milosevic, I believe that at no time-period was it the intention to terrorise the civilians and the civilian population and at no time was this the exclusive goal of everything that was happening throughout those years. I would very easily --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just concentrate on 1992/1993. Just concentrate on that and explain how what happened in 1992/1993 assists the argument you are putting forward in relation to terror in the indictment, which relates to the period 1994/1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I simply believe that through a witness of this type we can show what the combat activities were like in that period, 1992/1993 and I'm just taking the most flagrant examples of that. Because at the time it's quite certain that all the victims on either side were caused by the intensity of the combat actions. There was no other direct intention to harm civilians. This is what I always want to be heard from a witness who went through all of that, just to confirm that the combat actions between the two sides were the basis of the suffering of the civilian population, and I would also like to emphasise the time-period referring to Dragomir Milosevic, which in that time was in a flagrant way quite different and where any intention or any indication of an intention was ruled out, in terms of terrorising the civilians and sniping at the town for any reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll give a ruling when we return from the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, you may ask the question, and-- but let us move quickly to the period 1994/1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave I wanted to say something which has nothing to do with this witness. It has to do with the next witness, T-11, who can come here tomorrow and we have to conclude with him tomorrow due to his obligations. Four hours were foreseen for his testimony. I will do my utmost to shorten my examination since it's important -- although it is an important witness and there is a chance that we might not have him back any time soon. I also heard that the Prosecutor might have a significant number of questions for the cross-examination. Therefore, I believe with your permission, we should start tomorrow with witness T-11 first to try and deal with his testimony and to conclude with it in its entirety. The second application I have to make concerns Witness T-16. There's a request to take his testimony via videolink. As planned, it could take place on the 23rd. However, since the procedure of establishing the videolink is a lengthy one, could we please have your ruling as soon as possible. We submitted that request on the 29th of June. I don't know whether you received any response from the Prosecutor, but let us try and do everything in our power to be able to take that witness's testimony as planned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: For the latter we haven't yet received a response from the Prosecutor. Perhaps they will give it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We received the application. Although the witness entirely deals with 1992, the withdrawal of the JNA forces, we don't think it is relevant and I think relevancy is one of the aspects of having a videolink provided, but in -- as it -- in terms of the actual application, because there was a medical certificate attached, that's all fine. We don't have a problem, except for relevancy. That would be our response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you for that. The Chamber will dispose of that as quickly as possible. Perhaps by tomorrow. As for the first matter, it very much depends on the length of time that the parties spend questioning the witness, whether he will be able to -- to leave tomorrow. So that really is up to you, Mr. Tapuskovic, and the -- the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Trial Chamber and registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is very likely that we will not conclude this witness's testimony today, and in that case, his testimony or the rest of it would have to be transferred to Friday, together with the witness foreseen for Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see. You didn't make that clear. So what you're asking is for Witness T-11 to be interposed in the event that this witness's evidence is not concluded today. You're asking for him to be interposed. We will grant that request. Well, let us proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we discussed the event at Kula and the killing of those soldiers that were in detention. Can you explain to the Judges the following: You are a police inspector. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The witness never said there were soldiers that were killed in detention. He spoke only of detainees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. So rephrase the question, Mr. Tapuskovic. Because that is not a matter on which you can lead.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Don't argue, just go ahead. You don't have a point. Just rephrase the question. It was leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only refer back to the transcript because I believe the witness did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us again who was it that was killed in that incident?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I said that those were detainees from the VRS. On the orders of the military command they were detained because of certain infractions or violations they had made.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's how I understood your previous answer. As a police inspector, were you able to conduct any investigation? Were you asked to assist?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, since it was under the competence of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the army of Republika Srpska was able to do anything in order to investigate, for example, where the shell came from and how the incident actually happened?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that the shell came from the direction of Igman, although I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the end result of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It was in the hands of the military command. As the civilian police force, we had nothing to do there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It is necessary for us to move on. Let us go to 1994. Why -- or how do you remember the beginning of 1994?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Before do you that, just let me point out that of the one hour allotted to you, you have just two minutes remaining and you have -- you are now just reaching the portion of this witness's evidence that relates directly, directly to the indictment. You have spent an hour on 1992/1993, which is perhaps only marginally relevant, and the area, the aspects of the witness's evidence that relates directly to the indictment, you have left yourself no time to deal with that. Why are you so obsessed with 1992/1993? We'll grant you another -- we'll grant you -- how much more time would you need, considering that the time is virtually finished?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to conclude in 20 minutes, Your Honours. It is fully justified for you to ask me to explain the relevance of each witness's testimony, and then I focus on that, and that disturbs my schedule. Of course, I have to respond to each and every of your questions, but a lot of time was spent on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's true, yes. Yes, that's true. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let us quickly go through 1994. What happened then, do you remember? First of all, do you remember when Mr. Dragomir Milosevic was appointed commander of the SRK?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that Mr. Dragomir Milosevic came in the summer of that year, whether in late July or August 1994

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What happened in 1994 that had to do with heavy weapons?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that in the spring of 1994 in the area that we discussed from Lukavica and the surrounding places, the heavy weapons of the VRS were pulled out from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that Dragomir Milosevic took command of the SRK at that time you mentioned. Can you tell me what the period when he was in command looked like, in particular, since August and until the end of 1994?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: One can say that the situation was quite calm, there were no activities as they were in 1992 and 1993. There were sporadic provocations but no serious combat activities between the belligerent parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That calm period was interrupted by what? What happened in October that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I know very well that in the Trnovo theatre, that is in the demilitarised zone where the peace keeping forces were between the warring parties, the Serb army and the army of B and H, in October, there was a sabotage attack. The command of the Trnovo battalion was attacked. I think 21 soldiers were killed out of which three were nurses. They were members of the battalion. Although it was a demilitarised zone, they attacked. As far as I recall, only one girl survived. She was a radio person, and another soldier from the command of the Trnovo battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were you asked to assist in any regard as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: As policemen, we were asked to assist, we were ordered to do so. As a crime inspector, I went there as a soldier to protect the area where the attack had been carried out on the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you briefly tell the Judges in October, November, and December, did you do something else instead of your police duties?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In November and December of 1994, we were made part of the VRS, tasked with the defence of the lines there on the slopes of Bijelasnica and Treskavica, facing Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did the situation change during the combat operations then?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In December, on the 13th of December, to be exact, there was a fierce attack on the lines of the VRS by the army of BiH, whereupon a large number of casualties occurred. The VRS forces were pushed back in depth towards Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me when the situation calmed -- calmed down during that fall and winter?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The new combat positions, or the new line of the VRS, had been pushed back by eight or nine kilometres. After that fierce attack and the losses we suffered, the lines were re-established on the part of the VRS and there was no combat activity of any significance until late spring 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us move on to that period. What happened in the spring of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In June, July and August and until the end of the war, there were constant attacks by the ABiH on the defence positions of the VRS. Often these attacks were followed by heavy artillery shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember end May in particular for any reason?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: There was another strong attack and certain positions of the VRS were moved back. There was a counterattack, and we eventually managed to regain some positions. However, the VRS sustained a number of losses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to show you DD00-1757 next. Once it is before you, please look at the heading, the date, the nature of the document, and read the first paragraph out loud for the Chamber. After that, perhaps you can tell us whether you recognise any similarity in the document and the things you have mentioned in the past few minutes.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: "Sarajevo, the 1st of June -- Sarajevo, the 1st of June, 1995, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the army of the BiH republic, command of the 1st Corps, PKM, Bjela Vijeska, strictly confidential 011-191, Bileska 31st of May, 1995, time 2200 hours. Interim combat report." I think that's what the abbreviation is. "On the 30th of May, 1995, at 0500 hours joint units of the 1st corps with Special Units of MUP, Bosna and Lasta, in quotation marks, began attack combat actions along the axis of Voluja Jama, Djokin Toranj, Ilijas, Kozija Luka, Lopoc, Turov Stan, Pester, Kozljen, Cardak, and the village of Dujmovici."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell the Judges if you had anything to do with this -- if this has anything to do with what you told us earlier?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does have something to do with what I said before, because when the attack came, the next day we were engaged as police officers. The order was to go and assist members of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you look at the paragraph that is two paragraphs lower, which begins "During the fighting that lasted the whole day." Can you please read that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: "During the fighting that lasted for the whole day, at all four routes of attack" --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please, let's not waste time. I asked you to skip those two paragraphs and to read at the lower passage which begins "during the fighting that lasted all day." You can read that.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: "Throughout the fighting that lasted all day, the Chetniks sustained serious losses in personnel and materiel and equipment and large number of firing points were destroyed, bunkers, two trucks, passenger cars. The exact number of Chetniks that were taken out of combat was difficult to evaluate, while two dead Chetniks remained at liberated Koslin."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you look at the end of the document. This is just in front of the numbers that were being mentioned. During yesterday --

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I lost my text. "In the course of yesterday and part of today, a considerable amount -- quantity of ammunition was spent as well as materiel and equipment which needs to be replenished."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please look at who signed the document? This is on the following page.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Commander General Vahid Karavelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All of this that you read and what you have told us, does that correspond to what was happening during those two days when you were with the police unit in the action of the army, when you joined the army action?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: All of this is correct. It's just that a large -- there was a large number of casualties on the Republika Srpska side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we admit this document, please as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's absolutely nothing that's been elicited so far that would link this document to anything that went on in Trnovo municipality other than the witness saying it corresponds. We don't know where a single one of these locations, and there are a number of locations that may or may not be relevant, where on the map they're found, if they're in Ilijas or someplace far and away outside of Sarajevo. So without some basic foundation, I'd suggest it's irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, I would have to seek the explanation from the witness. He's going to tell you where the lines were, because Ilijas is mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: However, Witness, can you please tell Their Honours if these locations have anything to do with Trnovo or with the area of responsibility of the SRK in general, during this conflict in May?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: All of these locations are in the Trnovo municipality. They don't have anything to do with Ilijas, and they were in the area of responsibility of the SRK.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you can indicate each one on the map, but I'm not going to ask you to do that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I find my way around a map with great difficulty. But I do know all of the places where all these things were taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, may I ask a question of clarification. You yourself took part in these combat activities, since you said that the authorities had ordered to you join the troops on the front lines. Could you please tell me where specifically you were sent and if you fought with the soldiers so that we can establish that you were an eye-witness to these events? Where did you fight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We fought in the area of Dujmovici. We were there to assist the army of Republika Srpska, because there were considerable losses and the lines were broken in certain locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The location you mention is therefore part of the positions that we've just mentioned in the document that we've just read. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will be admitted as D284.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this was in May. Can you now please tell us what happened in the following months and if the conflict -- well, I don't want it qualify it. Anyway, what happened later?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Later, throughout the whole of July and August, and especially in October, from the 10th -- from the 2nd to the 10th of October, there were intense attacks along the lines of the defence of the army of Republika Srpska. I was a participant in the month of October. Near the village of Turovi where our lines were the police held those lines. It was awful, with what force and what artillery they battered our positions. I could even say that the earth was aflame from the artillery attacks. During the first two days, the artillery of the army of Republika Srpska to a -- acted with a smaller force but then in the ensuing days the artillery of the army of the Republika Srpska began to fire and the lines remained unchanged until the end of the fighting. I think that the fighting ended on the 10th of October, 1995, in those areas, in the area of Trnovo. In that period, Trnovo itself was shelled which had a civilian population and from what I recall, four civilians were killed, three women and one man. There were a large number of wounded civilians. The buildings were set on fire from the projectiles, houses and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me this finally. Let me ask you, when you were in Kula at the police outpost and you said that there were detained soldiers of the army of Republika Srpska in Kula, can you please tell us if there were any other detainees, especially in this period of 1994 and 1995, that is related to the period when Mr. Dragomir Milosevic was at this position?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: During that period, there were arrested or detained members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina held in the Kula prison. It wasn't such a large number of them but there were some and I know that most of them were very quickly exchanged in 1995 and 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were they exposed to any kind of mistreatment or abuse?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I really couldn't say. The prison was a separate institution and from what I know, from the prison guards there is was no mistreatment. The kitchen worked to feed both the civilian and the military staff, the prison staff, and the first shift to have lunch would be the civilian and the prison staff, and then there would be a second shift. There would be the prisoners of the army of Republika Srpska and then in the following shift the same restaurant was used by the detained members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ivanovic. My name is Carolyn Edgerton, like you've heard, and I'm going to ask you some questions based on what you've testified to today, but if you don't understand anything or if I'm not clear, please say. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, normally in the ICTY before a witness testifies, the lawyer for that -- working with that witness has to provide some information about the witness's testimony to the other side. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, did you know that the information I received about you actually doesn't say you were chief of the SUP in Trnovo before the war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we first provided information that we believed was sufficient a few days ago or when we were asked by the Prosecution. We immediately furnished the requested information, so a few days ago we did provide that information. Really, it was very difficult at the preparation stage to give more information than we did. The first time that I spoke with the witness in detail was over the past few days because I couldn't speak with him in more detail before. There wasn't time. So I wasn't able to take all the information about him. I presented that to you today, and when I was asked the day before yesterday, or whenever that was, to provide this information, I quickly did so.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, I'm not fond of this type of questioning. I don't see the need for it. I mean, how is he to know whether the information provided by Mr. Tapuskovic to you included information about his -- his status?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honours, I think my friend has completely misunderstood the objective of my question. It in no way cast -- or was meant to cast any aspersions on Mr. Tapuskovic and he did provide information when information was requested. I was asking this of the witness on a matter that might go to the witness's credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But how is he to know, I mean, unless you're going to put it to him that that is information which he never gave Mr. Tapuskovic. But how is he to know whether the information that Mr. Tapuskovic gave you included information about his particular status?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Fine, Your Honour. I'll rephrase the question. I'll put the question in a different way, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivanovic, you said that the police in Trnovo in the period leading up to the war worked together; in fact, until after the 21st and 22nd of April 1992. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: But, in fact, your appointment as chief of the police for the Serbian municipality of Trnovo pre-dated these events by more than three weeks, didn't it, or by three weeks?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, that is not correct. On the 21st of April, when the police -- Serb police split off from the police station at the request of the Serb policemen and with the approval of the SDS, I assumed the duties of the chief of the Serb police.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: But were you not formally appointed to the position of chief of the Serb police of Trnovo by the minister of the interior, Mico Stanisic, on the 1st of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: If we're talking about the 1st of April, 1992, I was not appointed by Minister Mico Stanisic because we were still a joint police station in Trnovo. And until this event, the attack of the Green Berets on the police, it was a joint police station, and Ekrem Gudinjak was the chief. He was an ethnic Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I ask we see document 03364 on the screen, please. Do you see the document dated 1st of April, 1992 that appears on the left-hand side of the -- pardon me, the right-hand side of the screen in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now am I correct if I say that this document is a decision by Mico Stanisic, Minister of the Interior, assigning you to the tasks and duties of the chief of the Trnovo SJB?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The document is correct. But I never received this document. I state this with a full authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you had -- even though you were an employee and became an employ, I should say, of the Serb ministry of the interior, you had no knowledge of Minister Stanisic's appointment of you?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I really did not know that Minister Mico Stanisic appointed me as chief. And I never received this decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it also correct that by -- in your capacity as chief of the police for the Serbian municipality of Trnovo, you were a member of the Crisis Staff for that municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to this function, yes, I was a member of the Crisis Staff as of the 21st of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And the purpose of the Crisis Staff, Mr. Ivanovic, was to organise the Serbs in Trnovo, wasn't it, to deal with both civilian and military issues.

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The goal of the Crisis Staff was to protect the Serbian population in that area. In the municipality of Trnovo, we were a minority. There was 29 per cent of the Serbian population in the municipality of Trnovo. The idea was to protect our families and our hearts.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So I take it from your answer, sir, you're not disagreeing with me when I put it to you the purpose of the Crisis Staff was to organise the Serbs, dealing with both civilian and military issues. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: As the police, we dealt with mostly civilian matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: My question was to the purpose of the Crisis Staff to organise the Serbs dealing with both civilian and military issues. Now you have sat on the Crisis Staff, so surely you would be in a position to speak to its basic objectives, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The main purpose of Crisis Staff was to protect the population from possible conflicts, attacks. That was the main issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now your job, the job of the Crisis Staff, was in fact to put into effect the instructions for the organisation and operations of Serbian people in emergency conditions issued by the SDS party on 19 December, 1991, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was not in any sort of leadership position in the SDS, so I don't know anything about that order or the instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I could have document 3362 brought up, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can you see the document. It is handwritten that appears on the right-hand side of the screen in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now would you agree that document reads that it's minutes of the extraordinary session of the Trnovo SDS on 25 December 1991 and under item 1, instructions for organising the Serbian people in crisis situations Radivoje Draskovic read out those instructions. You said earlier, sir, you were a member of the Crisis Staff. Are you saying that you were unaware of those instructions, given that they were read out at a meeting of the Trnovo SDS by Radivoje Draskovic?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do declare that I did not attend this meeting and that until the 21st of April, 1992, I was not part of the SDS Crisis Staff or had any duties in the Serbian Democratic Party of the Trnovo municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Wasn't Mr. Draskovic president of the Crisis Staff, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Draskovic was the president of Serbian Democratic Party of the municipality of Trnovo. I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Who then was the president of the Crisis Staff, sir? Who headed the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that as the party president it was Mr. Draskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Draskovic, who you served on the Crisis Staff with, never discussed with you these instructions for the organisation of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Never, never. For as long as I was -- well, until the 21st of April when the police split, for as long as I was a policeman in the joint police force until the 21st of April 1992 it was never mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you're asserting these instructions were never mentioned, even though, sir, you were also a member of the Territorial Defence command for Trnovo municipality, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RADE IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was not in the TO command. The Territorial Defence comprised soldiers in the reserve and the TO organisation was under the competence of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: There's a technical problem in the transcript. It's stopped running.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It has stopped running. Is that what you were going to say, Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to remark on something. I have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I make an inquiry from the technical staff as to what has happened to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We do have another, what, six and a half, seven minutes before the close of the day's proceedings. Is it back? Has it returned? No.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: These things happen, Your Honour. I suppose we can be grateful that it didn't happen much earlier in the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand that it will take another three minutes to correct this fault. In that event, Mr. Tapuskovic, you will have to hold your objection until Friday, Friday morning at 8.00. And -- but this witness will not be here tomorrow. Can the witness hear me?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, you understand that Mr. Tapuskovic, the counsel for the accused, asked that another witness be heard tomorrow and the Chamber granted that request. You will therefore return to court on Friday morning at 8.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.
